answer: Rhythm-Gated Identity Admission. Each identity must submit a short fixed-cadence message train; the network admits only trains whose inter-arrival variance stays within a narrow grove of allowed timing shapes, and rotates the cadence target at each epoch zenith. A joiner must hold that traffic shape for several epochs before a beacon grants standing. An attacker pays sustained per-identity bandwidth and timing discipline: mass parallel sybils either drift off cadence or need real machines locked to each schedule.
